summary: Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram is a historian, numismatist, and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer. He served in various curatorial and directorial roles at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and as vice president of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Michael Aris was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied at Durham University and SOAS under David Llewellyn Snellgrove. He held positions at St John's College, Wolfson College, St Antony's College, Harvard, and as professor at Oxford.
Michael Balk worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was a doctoral student at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Prussian State Library (attested 1991).

Michael Baxandall was an art historian educated at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, as Slade Professor at Oxford, and as professor at the Courtauld Institute, UC Berkeley, and Cornell.

Michael Bernays studied at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums, Bonn, and Heidelberg, studying under Adolf Holtzmann. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).

Michael Carrithers is an anthropologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Wesleyan and Oxford, he taught at Wolfson College, the London School of Economics, Oxford, and Durham University, where he became Professor of Anthropology in 1992.

Michael Chase is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Victoria and École Pratique des Hautes Études. He worked as an ancient philosophy researcher at CNRS (2001–2009) and Centre Jean Pépin, and serves as adjunct professor at Victoria.

Michael Comans works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and completed his studies under Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University, later serving as a faculty member at the University of Sydney.

Michael Como specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied with Carl Bielefeldt, Kuo-liang Wang, and Bernard Faure, and held a post at Columbia University (attested 2009).

Michael Eido Luetchford is a Buddhist studies and philosophy writer who earned an electronic engineering degree at the University of Bradford (~1963–1967). He studied traditionally under Gudō Wafu Nishijima (~1973–2007) and founded Windbell Publications.

Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich, where he was also a wissenschaftlicher Assistent. He was later appointed professor at the University of Hamburg (1994–2021) and founded the European Association for the Study of Chinese Manuscripts.

Michael Gregory Morony is a historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (BA) and the University of California, Los Angeles (MA), where he served as a professor beginning in 1974.

Michael Hahn was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Wilhelm Rau and earned his PhD at the University of Marburg. He held posts at the University of Bonn and Marburg, serving as chair of Indology and Tibetology at Marburg (1988–2007).
Michael Hookham is a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied traditionally under Chögyam Trungpa and Dilgo Khyentse, and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt specializes in Indology and linguistics. Educated at SOAS and University College London, he held posts at SOAS as a postdoctoral fellow, Head of the South Asia Department, and Associate Dean, as well as chair of the Britain-Nepal Academic Council.

Michael J. Sweet worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Richard Hugh Robinson. He later served as a clinical assistant professor in psychiatry at Wisconsin.
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned his Master of Arts at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko (attested 2011).

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Cape Town and earned his MA and doctoral degrees at the University of California, Santa Barbara under William F. Powell.
